cases.name: Plain item - happy path, no pricing carrier
cases.summary: 1 create → 200 New · no pricing push · 1 row

checks.label: Eton answers the create
checks.what: HTTP status of the create response

checks.label: Read the marker in the reply
checks.what: Status / ErrorCode / ErrorMessages[0] in the body

checks.label: Write the order to the database
checks.what: rows in the `orders` table for this order

checks.label: Send the price detail to Eton

cases.note: shopee_vn normally carries pricing. This is the case where it does not, so it proves buildShopeePayload returning empty skips the push rather than sending an empty or zeroed payload.
cases.given: A shopee_vn order with one plain item and no data.order_adjustment block.
then: Eton accepts the create and answers Status 'New'.
One row is written to orders.
No price detail is pushed — price_details.json must not grow.

cases.name: Shopee - order_adjustment pricing
cases.note: Shopee is the only channel carrying pricing at order level rather than per line. Proves that carrier is found and mapped.
cases.given: A shopee_vn order carrying its pricing in data.order_adjustment.adjustments.
then: Eton accepts the create, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
One price detail push, accepted 200, with the order-level Shopee components populated.

cases.name: Lazada - line_item_details
cases.note: The per-line carrier is a different shape from Shopee's. Proves the mapper reads it.
cases.given: A lazada_vn order carrying pricing per line, in order_items[].line_item_details.
then: Create accepted, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
One price detail push, accepted, carrying the per-line breakdown with Items[].SKU = SKU-ETON-001.

cases.name: TikTok - line_item_details
cases.note: Lazada and TikTok share one reader. Proves channel prefix resolution routes both to it, so a change made for one cannot silently break the other.
cases.given: A tiktok_vn order carrying pricing per line — the same shape Lazada uses.
then: Create accepted, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
One price detail push, accepted, carrying the per-line breakdown.

cases.name: TikTok - flat fallback (empty line_item_details)
cases.note: hasLineItemPricing has to fall back to the flat fields rather than read an empty array as 'no pricing'. Proves the fallback fires.
cases.given: A tiktok_vn order whose line_item_details is empty, but whose item_price and paid_price are non-zero.
then: Create accepted, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
One price detail push, accepted, mapped flat from item_price and paid_price with no line breakdown.

cases.name: TikTok - zero prices, nothing to push (boundary)
cases.note: The boundary between 'flat fallback' and 'no data'. Zeros pushed to Eton would assert the order had no discount, tax or shipping — silent corruption, not a visible failure. Proves pushPricingIfMapped skips instead.
cases.given: A tiktok_vn order whose line_item_details is empty AND whose item_price and paid_price are both zero.
then: Create accepted, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
No price detail call is made at all.

cases.name: Haravan - out of scope channel
cases.note: The important negative. An out-of-scope channel must skip pricing rather than send zeros, for the same reason as N6.
cases.given: A haravan_vn order. Channel resolution is longest-prefix over EtonConstants.SalesChannel.BY_MARKETPLACE_PREFIX, and only Shopee, Lazada and TikTok are in scope, so resolveChannel returns null.
then: Create accepted, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
No price detail call is made at all.

cases.name: Packed order
cases.note: Cancellation behaviour later keys off packed state — cancelOrder reads any 400 as 'Eton packed it'. Proves creation records that state in the first place.
cases.given: An order whose number contains PACKED, which makes the mock answer as a warehouse that has already packed it.
then: Create accepted with Status 'Packed' rather than 'New'.
One row in orders.
The code is appended to packed_orders.json.
No price detail push.

cases.name: Replay - Eton answers BESO05 already exists
cases.note: A replay must not be read as an error and must not duplicate the row. Proves handleAlreadyExistsOnEton takes the replay branch.
cases.given: An order whose number contains EXISTS, so Eton answers 400 with error code BESO05 — meaning it already holds this order.
then: The create answers 400 carrying BESO05.
createOrder treats that as success, not failure.
The order is not re-saved — one row in orders, not two.
The price detail push still goes out and is accepted.

cases.name: Eton 500 - retry then recover
cases.note: Proves a 5xx is retried rather than swallowed, and that nothing is persisted for an order Eton never accepted. The unsynchronized report cannot be proven here unless event_name is order_creation — see the known gap.
cases.given: An order whose number contains SERVERERROR, so Eton answers 500 to every create attempt.
then: Exactly 3 create calls, 30 seconds apart — @Retryable's contract.
No row is written to orders.
No price detail push.
After the third attempt @Recover runs.

cases.name: Eton 400 generic - reported unsynchronized
cases.expected: create x1 -> 400, 'Validation failed', pricing x0, db 0
cases.note: A 4xx means the payload is wrong; retrying it three times would only delay the report. Proves the integration tells 4xx and 5xx apart.
cases.given: An order whose number contains INVALID, so Eton answers a generic 400 rather than BESO05.
then: Exactly 1 create call — a 400 is not retried.
No row in orders.
No price detail push.
The order is reported unsynchronized to OMS on the pushUnsynchronizedOrder queue.

cases.name: Pricing rejected - whole run replays
cases.note: The most valuable case in the suite — the only one exercising 'the order exists on Eton but its pricing does not'. The one-row assertion is what proves handleAlreadyExistsOnEton skips the save on replay. Against a stateless mock every attempt is answered 200 and the integration writes three rows, which is a mock artefact rather than a defect.
cases.given: An order whose id contains 9666, so Eton accepts the create but rejects the price detail with 400. The marker sits on the id, not the number, because the pricing push is addressed by the code Eton echoed back — and DataDTO.order_id is a Long, so it had to be numeric.
then: 3 create calls and 3 pricing calls — the pricing failure throws inside the create path, so the whole run replays.
The first create answers 200; the next two answer 400 BESO05, because the mock remembers what it created.
Exactly one row in orders, not three.

cases.name: Empty order_items - mock validation 400
cases.expected: create x1 -> 400, 'must not be empty', pricing x0, db 0
cases.note: The array is sent empty rather than omitted on purpose: omitting the key NPEs inside buildCreateSaleOrderItems before any Eton call is made, which would test nothing.
cases.given: An order with an empty order_items array, which produces an empty ListSODetail. Eton's schema forbids it.
then: The create answers 400 naming 'ListSODetail' must not be empty.
1 create call — not retried.
No row in orders.
No price detail push.

cases.name: Shopee kit - explodes into components
cases.note: Eton has no concept of a kit. Proves the explosion happens before the payload is built, and that the quantity arithmetic multiplies through.
cases.given: A shopee_vn order for a kit, quantity 2, made of two components.
then: ListSODetail carries one line per component, not one line for the kit — 1025377-A quantity 6, 1025377-B quantity 2, i.e. component quantity × kit quantity.
Create accepted, Status 'New'.
One row in orders.
One price detail push with one Items[] entry per component.

cases.name: TikTok kit - line_item_details carrier
cases.note: Kit explosion and per-line pricing have to compose. Proves neither breaks the other.
cases.given: The same kit, on a tiktok_vn order carrying its pricing per line.
then: Components exploded exactly as in K1.
Create accepted; one row in orders.
One price detail push, mapped from line_item_details.

cases.name: Kit and plain item in one order
cases.note: Proves explosion is per line rather than per order: a plain line sitting beside a kit must survive untouched.
cases.given: One order holding a kit of two components and a plain item.
then: ListSODetail carries 3 lines — the 2 components and INV-PLAIN.
Create accepted; one row in orders.
One price detail push.

cases.name: Kit with a component missing its SKU - validation 400
cases.expected: create x1 -> 400, 'SKU' is required', pricing x0, db 0
cases.note: A shape-specific failure a plain item cannot produce. The index in Eton's error names the exploded line, which is what proves the component reached Eton as a line of its own.
cases.given: A kit whose second component has no SKU.
then: The create answers 400 naming 'ListSODetail[1].SKU' is required.
1 create call — not retried.
No row in orders.
No price detail push.
